page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is built on an x86_64 architecture featuring the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 96 physical cores across 2 threads per core. Memory allocation totals 768.0 GB, retaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache, alongside support for AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI. It does not include dedicated GPUs or local storage, relying entirely on remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results show exceptional throughput in highly parallelized computing tasks. Multi-core performance reaches the top 10% tier in stress-ng with a score of 194,674.5, complemented by a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 148,946.94 and strong extended instruction handling. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 879.52 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput hits 156.95 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Memory subsystem bandwidth is high under uncached read conditions at 673.92 GB/sec and uncached write at 269.25 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects baseline middle-tier outcomes, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 2,239.79.

In data-intensive and in-memory operations, the instance demonstrates high concurrency capabilities, achieving 263.82 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and top-tier metrics for PassMark database operations. For machine learning tasks, CPU-based prompt evaluation across small (135M), medium (7B), and large (70B) language models registers in the top 25%. However, text generation speeds drop to average or weak percentiles due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. Given its resource density and absence of bundled local disks, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise services, multi-tenant container fleets, and enterprise databases requiring significant thread concurrency alongside remote storage attachments.

It provides 192 dedicated vCPUs from 96 physical cores, 768.0 GB of RAM, and 480 MB of L3 cache, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs or local storage.
